name: neonmeter
description: Neon rate-limit and context meter for Claude Code, drawn above the prompt

barColoring.title: Bar coloring
barColoring.description: level colors every filled cell by the segment's percent; ramp runs the filled part through every range up to the percent's in equal stretches

layout.title: Layout
layout.description: all draws every segment in one row; single draws one segment across the whole row and takes turns: 5-hour, Weekly (each weekly limit), Spend, Context

desktopBars.title: Desktop bars
desktopBars.description: How bars draw in the desktop app: a smooth glowing bar with rounded ends, or a row of glowing dots

pulse.title: Pulse
pulse.description: Pulse live cells and percents in their own color; off draws them still

glow.title: Glow
glow.description: Draw the desktop's halo under filled bars, dots and percents; off draws them crisp (the pulse still brightens them)

pulseMode.title: Pulse mode
pulseMode.description: responsive pulses pulseCount cycles each time a value changes (a percent, the context, staleness) and otherwise holds the glow still, which costs next to nothing; always pulses without a stop, which costs about a fifth of a CPU core in the desktop app

pulseCount.title: Pulses per change
pulseCount.description: How many pulse cycles pulseMode responsive runs each time a value changes, 1 to 20

pulseMs.title: Pulse cycle (ms)
pulseMs.description: Length of one pulse cycle in milliseconds, 400 to 3000

segments.title: Segments
segments.description: Which segments to draw and in what order: five_hour, seven_day, spend, context (spend shows only when the account reports a spend limit)

pollSeconds.title: Poll interval (s)
pollSeconds.description: Seconds between usage fetches, 10 to 3600; a reading older than twice this is marked stale

theme.title: Theme
theme.description: auto follows Claude Code's theme setting (dark when it cannot be read); dark or light forces that palette

desktopTheme.title: Desktop theme
desktopTheme.description: Palette in the desktop app: auto follows the app's own light or dark appearance (and the system theme it follows), dark or light overrides it

ranges.title: Range bounds
ranges.description: Where each of the six color ranges starts: five ascending whole numbers from 1 to 99, separated by commas

colorsDark.title: Colors (dark)
colorsDark.description: The six range colors on a dark background, lowest range first, as #RRGGBB

colorsLight.title: Colors (light)
colorsLight.description: The six range colors on a light background, lowest range first, as #RRGGBB

glyph.title: Bar cell
glyph.description: The character every terminal bar cell is drawn with: one single-width character such as ━ ● ■ █ • (wide characters and emoji are refused; the desktop draws vectors)

rotateSeconds.title: Weekly rotation (s)
rotateSeconds.description: Seconds each weekly limit shows when the Weekly segment rotates between several, and each segment shows in the single layout, 2 to 60

fiveHourReset.title: 5-hour reset
fiveHourReset.description: How the 5-hour window's reset shows on the widest layout: countdown is the time left (in 3h13m), clock the time it resets (14:05); narrower layouts always count down

weeklyReset.title: Weekly reset
weeklyReset.description: How every weekly limit's reset (all models and each model's, such as Fable) shows on the widest layout: countdown is the time left, as the 5-hour window shows it (in 2d15h, in 8h50m), clock the day and time it resets (Thu 14:05); narrower layouts always count down

resetColor.title: Reset color
resetColor.description: plain draws each window's reset in the text color; time colors it by how much of the window is still to run, on the same six colors and ranges as the percents (a reset that is close is blue, one far off red), with the pulse and the desktop's glow, faded when stale; timeRanges sets where each color starts

timeRanges.title: Time range bounds
timeRanges.description: Where each of the six colors starts for resetColor time, as the share of the window still to run: five ascending whole numbers from 1 to 99, separated by commas; the default splits the window into six even steps

contextBar.title: Context bar
contextBar.description: breakdown splits the context bar into its categories in neon, as the desktop app's own context indicator does (Messages, System tools, MCP tools, Skills, Other, then the autocompact buffer in grey); percent colors it by its percent like every other bar

contextPopup.title: Context breakdown on hover
contextPopup.description: In the desktop app, show the context breakdown (each category's tokens and share of the window, in its color) while the pointer is over the Context segment

contextColorsDark.title: Context colors (dark)
contextColorsDark.description: The six context category colors on a dark background, as #RRGGBB: Messages, System tools, MCP tools, Skills, Other, Autocompact buffer

contextColorsLight.title: Context colors (light)
contextColorsLight.description: The six context category colors on a light background, as #RRGGBB: Messages, System tools, MCP tools, Skills, Other, Autocompact buffer

compactButton.title: Compact button
compactButton.description: A round button colored by the context percent that compacts the conversation, as /compact does: appear shows it once the context reaches compactAt, always whenever the context has a reading, off never

compactAt.title: Compact button appears at (%)
compactAt.description: The context percent from which compactButton appear shows the button, 1 to 100

compactPosition.title: Compact button position
compactPosition.description: outside-right and outside-left put the button beside the row, which keeps its own layout whatever it shows; end, context and start put it inside the row, after the last segment, before the Context segment or before the first, taking room from the bars

compactGlow.title: Compact button glow
compactGlow.description: Draw the compact button's halo in the desktop app; glow off draws none either way

compactPulse.title: Compact button pulse
compactPulse.description: Pulse the compact button with the band; pulse off holds it still either way
